questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What would explain why the transition from a planned economy to a market economy often results in a decrease in national output in the short run?

options.A: an accompanying decrease in inward investment
options.B: an accompanying decrease in the wish to save
options.C: an accompanying increase in inward migration
options.D: an accompanying increase in structural unemployment

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a person’s marginal costs and marginal benefits of making trips to the cinema. costs, benefits marginal cost ($) marginal benefit 0 1 2 3 4 number of trips How many trips will the person make?

options.A: None, as each extra trip reduces marginal benefit.
options.B: One, as this maximises the excess of marginal benefit over marginal cost.
options.C: Two, as this maximises the net benefit of making trips.
options.D: Three, as all trips have a positive marginal benefit.

questions.questionText: A number of changes occur in an economy. Online training is made available to engineers, machinery in food processing is automated, profit taxes are imposed on information technology entrepreneurs and subsidised fertilisers are given to farmers. Which factor of production is least likely to experience rising productivity?

options.A: capital
options.B: enterprise
options.C: labour
options.D: land

questions.questionText: What is correct about market demand?

options.A: Market demand can increase only when all individuals increase their consumption.
options.B: Market demand for an inferior good falls as price falls.
options.C: Market demand is effective when consumers desire to buy the good.
options.D: Market demand is the result of aggregating the demand of all individuals.

questions.questionText: D D shows an individual’s initial demand curve for public transport.

A theatre increases the price of its tickets from $5 to $10. As a result, its total receipts increase from $2500 to $4000. Within what range does the price elasticity of demand for theatre tickets lie?

The table shows how an individual’s weekly consumption of biscuits and coffee varies with income. income ($) biscuits (packs) coffee (cups) 100 0 5 150 5 10 Which statement about the income elasticity of demand over the range of income shown is true?

options.A: For biscuits it is greater than 1.
options.B: For biscuits it is zero.
options.C: For coffee it is less than 1.
options.D: For coffee it is unitary.

questions.questionText: The diagrams show changes in the market for a good.
A product has a high price elasticity of supply. What might explain this?

options.A: The product has a high opportunity cost.
options.B: The product has a non-perishable nature.
options.C: The product is classed as an inferior good.
options.D: The product is considered to be a luxury.

questions.questionText: The market for onions is in equilibrium. A disease strikes the onion crop and new health benefits of consuming onions are discovered. Which combination of changes in demand and supply matches these events? demand supply

options.A: falls falls
options.B: falls rises
options.C: rises falls
options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a competitive market in equilibrium with price P and quantity Q. X S price P Y Z D O Q quantity Which area shows the consumer surplus and which area shows the producer surplus? consumer producer surplus surplus

options.A: OXYQ OZYQ
options.B: OXYQ PYZ
options.C: XYP OZYQ
options.D: XYP PYZ

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for a good. S P P price D O Q Q Q
People walking past a bakery often comment on the pleasure of smelling freshly baked bread. Of what is this an example?

options.A: a negative consumption externality
options.B: a negative production externality
options.C: a positive consumption externality
options.D: a positive production externality

questions.questionText: When would cost-benefit analysis definitely indicate that a government project should be approved?

options.A: if it eliminated all external costs
options.B: if it gave a higher rate of return than a private sector project
options.C: if it maximised net social benefit
options.D: if it minimised total social cost

questions.questionText: The table gives information about the 2011 Australian Grand Prix in Australian dollars (AUD). AUD (millions) costs of operating the Grand Prix 85 revenue from sales of tickets and sponsorship 32 external costs e.g. noise, congestion etc. net of external benefits 4 consumer surplus for those attending the Grand Prix 6 What was the value of the welfare outcome of holding the Australian Grand Prix?

options.A: –AUD49 million B –AUD51 million C –AUD53 million D –AUD63 million

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: A demerit good is overconsumed.
options.B: A demerit good produces zero consumer surplus.
options.C: A merit good is defined by its non-excludability and non-rivalry.
options.D: A merit good is provided free of charge.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves of a good. S J price D O quantity The government sets a minimum price of OJ for the good. How will this affect the producers and consumers of the good? effect on producers effect on consumers

options.A: all producers will gain consumers will lose
options.B: all producers will gain consumers will gain
options.C: some producers will gain and some will lose consumers will lose
options.D: some producers will gain and some will lose consumers will gain

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual production per worker per year in three countries. There are no trade barriers, no transport costs and the countries specialise on the basis of opportunity cost. product (tonnes) Southland Westland Eastland yams 100 80 12 wheat 80 70 16 rice 60 60 8 Which country will export which product? Southland Westland Eastland

options.A: rice yams wheat
options.B: wheat rice yams
options.C: yams rice wheat
options.D: yams wheat rice

questions.questionText: What may limit the benefits a country derives from engaging in international trade?

options.A: The country is specialised in agricultural production.
options.B: The country’s labour force is highly immobile.
options.C: There are no product areas where the country enjoys an absolute advantage.
options.D: Wage rates are lower in the country’s principal competitors.

questions.questionText: The supply of an imported good is shown by curve S. What will be the new supply curve if an ad valorem (percentage) tariff is imposed on the good? A B S C price D O quantity
Trade relations between two countries have gone through four stages. At which stage was a customs union established?

options.A: The countries removed tariffs on selected goods from each other.
options.B: The countries removed tariffs on all goods from each other.
options.C: The countries set up a common external tariff towards other countries.
options.D: The countries introduced a single currency for use by both countries.

questions.questionText: The table gives the percentage (%) rates of youth unemployment and total unemployment in France and the UK in 2001 and 2005. France UK youth total youth total unemployment unemployment unemployment unemployment (%) (%) (%) (%) 2001 19.2 8.7 12.0 5.2 2005 22.1 10.1 12.5 4.8 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: France and the UK experienced the same trends in unemployment.
options.B: France had a higher number of unemployed people than the UK.
options.C: The UK used a different definition of unemployment from France.
options.D: The UK was more successful than France in controlling unemployment.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the original aggregate demand curve, AD , and the original aggregate supply curve, AS . What will be the new equilibrium if there is a fall in the country’s exports and an increase in government subsidies to firms? AS AS

options.A: AS
options.D: X B price level C AD AD AD O real output

questions.questionText: In June 2013, the Governor of the Bank of Namibia announced that the Central Bank’s lending rate would remain low as long as inflation remained low. What would not lead to a risk of inflation?

options.A: increased output in the mining, manufacturing and construction industries
options.B: Namibian dollar depreciation against the currencies of its trading partners
options.C: severe weather problems that harm crop production
options.D: the Namibian Government’s policy of increased public expenditure

questions.questionText: The capital value of a non-interest bearing asset is index-linked. During a period of inflation, how will its money value and its real value change? money value real value

options.A: rises rises
options.B: rises stays constant
options.C: stays constant falls
options.D: stays constant stays constant

questions.questionText: For many years, Japan had a current account surplus which then became a current account deficit. What might explain this change?

options.A: Japan has faced deflation.
options.B: Japan has introduced protectionist policies.
options.C: Japan’s currency has depreciated.
options.D: Japanese manufacturing has lost its comparative advantage.

questions.questionText: What is the likely effect on the volume of exports and imports if a country with a fixed exchange rate experiences a higher rate of inflation than its trading partners? exports imports

options.A: increase decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase increase
options.D: decrease decrease

questions.questionText: The graphs show the changes in the exchange rates of the £ sterling against the US$ and the Euro (€) between 2001 and 2003. US$ per £ £ per Euro 0.725 1.750 0.700 1.700 1.650 0.675 1.600 US$ € 0.650 1.550 0.625 1.500 1.450 0.600 1.400 0.575 2001 2002 2003 2001 2002 2003 What happened to the value of the £ sterling between 2001 and 2003?

options.A: The £ appreciated against the US$ and depreciated against the Euro .
options.B: The £ appreciated against the US$ and the Euro .
options.C: The £ depreciated against the US$ and appreciated against the Euro .
options.D: The £ depreciated against the US$ and the Euro .

options.A: to decrease a current account surplus
options.B: to decrease demand-pull inflation
options.C: to improve the terms of trade
